subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

items.answer: To move back and forth very fast

items.prompt: When you pluck a rubber band and it moves, what do you hear?

steps: The vibrating rubber band makes a sound.

items.prompt: If you stop a guitar string from moving, what happens to the sound?
Rice on a drum jumps when a loud sound is made. What does this show?

steps: The sound makes the drum vibrate, moving the rice.
Loud sound can make things like a drum vibrate.

items.prompt: When you hum, what vibrates in your body?

steps: Your throat vibrates to make the hum.

items.prompt: Does a vibrating ruler make a sound?

steps: A twanged ruler vibrates and makes a sound.

items.prompt: True or false: sound is made by vibrations.
What happens to the sound when the vibration gets faster or stronger?
items.answer: There is still a sound (it changes)

steps: Vibrations make sound; changing them changes the sound.

items.prompt: Explain why a plucked rubber band makes a sound.
items.answer: It vibrates, and vibrating makes sound

steps: The back-and-forth motion of the band creates the sound.

items.prompt: Describe a test to show that sound can make something vibrate.
items.answer: Put rice on a drum and make a loud sound near it to watch the rice jump

steps: The jumping rice shows the sound made the drum vibrate.

items.prompt: Why does a bell stop ringing when you hold it still?
items.answer: Holding it stops the vibration, so the sound stops

steps: No vibration means no sound from the bell.

items.prompt: Name one thing that vibrates to make a sound.
items.answer: A guitar string (or rubber band, drum, or your throat)

steps: Strings, rubber bands, and drums vibrate to make sound.

items.prompt: Plan a test to show that a vibrating object makes a sound.
items.answer: Pluck a rubber band and listen while it moves back and forth

steps: The vibrating band makes a sound you can hear.
